purpose: Revenue Publisher v2 - the reusable revenue-theme contract. Before this file existed, the publisher lane was shaped around one thesis (shadow-ai-spend-accountability). A vertical declares the buyer problem, which evidence families count, which audience is being written for, which VERIFIED existing asset the CTA must reach, and what may never be claimed. Adding a revenue theme is a record here plus evidence in acquisition/signal-intelligence/signals.json - not a code change.
selection_principle: demand_strength x purchase_intent x existing_asset_fit x freshness x measurement_quality / operational_burden. Exactly one opportunity is published at a time: the highest-scoring ACTIVE vertical with an eligible, unexpired candidate. Article count is never the objective.

state_meanings.ACTIVE: Evidence and a verified existing asset both support publishing into this vertical now.
state_meanings.WATCH: The thesis is legitimate but either the evidence or the existing-asset fit is not yet sufficient. Nothing is generated for a WATCH vertical.
state_meanings.RETIRED: No longer pursued. Kept for provenance.

verticals.buyer_problem: Unbudgeted AI and SaaS spend has to be justified with a defensible number before the next renewal or budget approval.
verticals.editorial_angle: Turn a vague productivity defence into a spend figure a reader can defend. Stay narrower than the general AI-workflow-ROI category, which the recorded evidence describes as saturated.

verticals.new_product_gate_reason: ai-saas-waste-calculator is LIVE and HTTP_VERIFIED and already answers the buyer problem.

verticals.buyer_problem: Individuals and small teams have accumulated AI subscriptions and cannot decide which ones to keep, downgrade, consolidate or cancel.
verticals.editorial_angle: A decision procedure, not a tool roundup. The reader should finish able to sort their own subscriptions into KEEP / DOWNGRADE / CONSOLIDATE / CANCEL using criteria that survive the cases where the obvious answer is wrong. Written for a solo operator or a small team, not for enterprise finance.
decision_dimensions: adequacy of a free or cheaper alternative

verticals.buyer_problem: Teams evaluating AI agents cannot state a payback period once human-review overhead is counted, so the purchase stalls at the business case.
verticals.editorial_angle: Payback arithmetic that survives review overhead. Not published until the evidence is corroborated by something other than an inherited assumption.

verticals.promotion_requires: At least one OBSERVED, external, independent signal specific to agent payback, from an independence group other than owned.

verticals.buyer_problem: Per-token and per-run AI costs are unpredictable, so operators cannot price work or set a budget ceiling with confidence.
verticals.editorial_angle: Runtime cost as an operating constraint rather than a pricing-page comparison. Deliberately held back: publishing this now would produce a fourth page competing with three existing spend pages for the same queries.
prohibited_claims: current per-token prices for any named provider
verticals.watch_reason: No thesis and no OBSERVED evidence records exist for this vertical yet, and the observed subscription-vs-API pricing posts sit in the same independence group as the subscription-rationalization evidence, so they cannot corroborate a separate runtime-cost thesis on their own. Promotion also requires a distinct existing-asset fit: the spend pages already cover the adjacent queries.
verticals.promotion_requires: Its own corroborated thesis with at least two external OBSERVED signals from different independence groups, plus an asset-fit result that is not already served by the ai_spend_accountability or ai_subscription_rationalization routes.
verticals.new_product_gate_reason: Nothing is built for a WATCH vertical.
